attempts.rationale: The series has strong seasonality but unstable model rankings (ranking_tau=-0.24) and high error correlation among top models. A robust combination like DBA or Trimmed Mean is appropriate to mitigate this instability. I will start by testing a simple Arithmetic Mean as a baseline for robustness.

A robust combination like DBA (Dynamic Bayesian Aggregation or similar robust aggregator) or trimmed mean can mitigate the impact of outlier errors from poorly performing models in specific windows. I will test a trimmed mean to reduce sensitivity to the worst-performing models which appear in different positions across validation windows.

The ranking instability (tau=-0.24) and high error correlation within model groups suggest that simple averaging is robust but potentially suboptimal compared to a weighted approach that accounts for recent performance trends. I will test `inverse_error` weighting on the top 8 models, which have shown consistent low error in the aggregate, to see if leveraging their relative stability improves over the unweighted mean.

The median is robust to outliers and model errors, which aligns with the "robust" combination hint and unstable ranking diagnosis.
